newsitem.title: USA: UAL sees higher Q2 fully distributed EPS.
newsitem.headline: UAL sees higher Q2 fully distributed EPS.

text.p: UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, said Tuesday it expects second quarter fully distributed earnings per share to be up slightly from a year earlier.
In the second quarter of 1996 UAL earned $2.52 per fully distributed share before debt repurchases.
UAL said it expects United's strong performance to continue in the second quarter. Industry fundamentals remain healthy despite the reimposition of a 10 percent ticket tax in early March, it said.

Based on that outlook, UAL said it expects a modest year-over-year increase in unit revenue and higher earnings in the second quarter. This would continue its trend of year-over-year improvements in quarterly results, it added.
UAL today reported first quarter earnings of $1.61 a share on a fully distributed basis, up from $0.72 a year ago before a debt extinguishment charge.

"Driving United's record first-quarter performance was our continued strong U.S. domestic passenger unit revenue growth, which outperformed the industry once again," UAL Chairman Gerald Greenwald said in a statement.
He said United had a record first quarter passenger load factor of 69.9 percent, up 1.2 percentage points from a year ago.
Operating revenues rose 10.3 percent to $4.1 billion.
Yield, based on passenger revenue per passenger mile, increased 4.7 percent to $0.128 from $0.1222 a year ago.
Available seat miles rose 3.6 percent to 40.32 billion from 38.92 billion. Revenue passenger miles gained 5.4 percent to 28.17 billion from 26.73 billion.
